# Vacībhedakathā (Kv 2.5)

**ID:** Kv 2.5  
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)

**Title (Pali):** Vacībhedakathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul9.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul9.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vacībhedakathā* (Kv 2.5) is the fifth discourse of the second chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Skorupski 1991]. The debate investigates the thesis that there can be vocal utterance or verbal articulation (*vacībheda*) on the part of a practitioner who is in a meditative attainment (*samāpanna*) [Skorupski 1991; Bareau 1955]. This dispute addresses the fifth thesis in the controversy over Mahādeva's five points, which asserted that entry into the noble path (*mārga*) by one in meditative absorption can be accompanied by an exclamation—specifically uttering the word "suffering" (*dukkha*) upon realizing suffering [Skorupski 1991; Lamotte 1988]. In the *Kathāvatthu*, the Theravādin refutation questions whether knowing suffering necessitates vocalizing the word [Skorupski 1991]. Sectarian doxographies by Bhavya and others ascribe this proposition to the Mahāsāṃghika and Ekavyavahārika traditions [Skorupski 1991; Bareau 1955].
